chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the testimony of women, is it valid in marriage? He said: 'Yes, and it is not valid in divorce.'
He said: And Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of women is valid in stoning when there are three men and two women, but when there are four women and two men, it is not valid in stoning.'
I said: 'Is the testimony of women valid with men in blood (diyah)?' He said: 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for women's testimony in marriage, divorce, stoning, and blood money according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the classical Shia juristic distinction between financial/contractual matters, where women's testimony is often equal to men's, and penal matters like stoning (Rajm) and blood money (Diyah), where it is restricted or invalid. It highlights the specific ratios required for Rajm, reflecting the principle that testimony in hudud cases demands higher evidentiary standards, while explicitly rejecting the validity of women's testimony in Diyah, a point of scholarly discussion regarding the nature of compensation. The narration underscores the nuanced application of Quranic verses on testimony across different legal domains within Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musny Al Hannat who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the testimony of the women, it is allowed regarding the marriage?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but it is not allowed regarding the divorce’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The testimony of the women is allowed regarding the stoning when there were three men and two women, but when there were four women and two men, so it is not allowed regarding the stoning’.
I said, ‘Is the testimony of the women allowed with the men regarding the blood?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Najran from Muthanna’ al-Hannat from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “
I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the testimony of women if it is acceptable in marriage. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is acceptable, but it is not acceptable about divorce.’

He (the Imam) said that Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Testimony of women is acceptable in stoning if there are three men and two women; but if there are four women and two men it is not acceptable about stoning.’
I asked, ‘Is testimony of women with men acceptable in blood (life) cases?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not acceptable.’”
